audit_findings.title: Completed Aydin acquisition is missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.5 million filed purchase price financed with approximately $24.5 million of borrowings; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition changes the OE perimeter, acquisition-funded interest, acquired liabilities, working capital, cash bridge and potentially the share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: The Delayed Draw Term Loan may only be used for permitted acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: A timing and perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: the valuation uses June 30 assets, cash and debt even though Aydin closed on July 21. Aydin earnings are omitted, which can understate value, while financing costs and other post-closing claims are omitted, which can overstate value. The net direction cannot be established without Aydin operating and closing data, but a $24.5 million transaction is reasonably capable of changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing statement, purchase-price adjustment, post-closing balance sheet and Aydin historical or pro-forma operating results; then rerun OE, cash, debt-related interest and fully diluted shares on one consistent post-closing perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Current debt interest burden may not be reflected in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Q3 FY2026 interest expense was $1.017 million, an annualized $4.068 million versus $1.725 million in FY2025—a computed $2.343 million pretax run-rate gap before Aydin interest
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is equity-level OE and debt principal is not deducted, all recurring interest and commitment fees must reduce forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, the Initial Term Loan had an effective interest rate of 7.0 % and the Revolving Facility had an effective interest rate of 8.0 %.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: the $16.3 million anchor retains FY2025 interest, while debt reached $54.5 million by June 30 and another approximately $24.5 million was borrowed for Aydin. Annualizing filed Q3 interest implies about $1.832 million of additional after-tax annual expense at the filed 21.8% nine-month tax rate; using the valuation's base-case capitalization, that is approximately $25.7 million or $1.38 per share before Aydin interest. The exact recurring burden remains unresolved, but it is clearly capable of materially reducing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile daily average debt through the Aydin closing, contractual spreads, the interest-rate swap, commitment fees and issuance-cost amortization; calculate recurring after-tax interest and rerun every scenario from normalized equity OE.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 anchor captures an explicitly temporary Honeywell production spike
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.0 million of FY2025 sales, equal to 36.8% of $84.3 million total sales; temporary sales and OE portions unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary revenue and margin contribution can overstate normalized anchor OE; lowering forecast growth does not correct an overstated starting level.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate this will lead to a spike in revenues in the short term followed by a temporary dip in revenues before revenues are normalized.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that FY2025 included the Honeywell product line during a management-described production spike, but it does not quantify how much of the $31.0 million was accelerated or its OE contribution. Because the affected sales were more than one-third of FY2025 revenue and the valuation capitalizes the full $16.3 million anchor even in the bear case, the normalization issue is reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain quarterly Honeywell-line revenue, gross profit, transition costs, working-capital investment and maintenance capital expenditure; derive a post-transition run-rate OE and rerun all scenarios using that normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: One-time ERTC income may remain in the recurring anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.515 million pretax net benefit; $1.186 million after tax at 21.7%, conditionally equivalent to approximately $0.76-$1.05 per share across the valuation scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: If included, the nonrecurring other-income benefit inflates anchor equity OE and every forecast and terminal-value cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: Other income was $1.5 million in fiscal year 2025, which was primarily from monies received of $1.9 million with respect to the Employee Retention Tax Credits (“ERTC”), offset by a $0.4 million one-time ERTC related settlement fee.
audit_findings.explanation: The ERTC benefit is demonstrably nonrecurring, but the supplied OE reconciliation does not establish whether it was included in the $16.3 million anchor. If included, the filed net benefit equals 9.3% of the anchor before tax and would reduce indicated value by roughly 7.3%, which is material to the valuation estimates even though it would reinforce rather than reverse the conclusion that price exceeds modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 OE reconciliation and trace the $1.894 million credit and $0.379 million related fee; if present, remove both consistently with their tax effects and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: All cash is treated as surplus despite substantial operating and acquisition uses
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum disputed bridge amount is $10.695 million, or $0.57 per diluted share; 4.5% of the $240 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for operations or post-closing obligations should be excluded from the surplus-cash equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s principal source of liquidity has been cash flows from current year operations and cash accumulated from prior years’ operations, supplemented with our revolving credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether all June 30 cash was genuinely excess is unresolved, particularly given inventory growth and acquisition integration. However, even removing the entire $10.695 million bridge addition would reduce values only to approximately $10.39, $12.27 and $14.48 per share in the bear, base and bull cases. Each remains below the $18.52 market price, so this item alone cannot change the valuation conclusion. The Aydin purchase itself was filed as debt-financed rather than funded from the reported cash balance.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum operating cash, restricted balances, post-closing cash and committed working-capital needs; adjust the bridge if necessary, without treating this item alone as conclusion-changing.

audit_findings.title: Anchor durability depends heavily on one defense program
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed FY2025 F-16 sales were approximately $30.9 million, or 36.7% of total sales; the subsequent nine-month filing reports a $10.8 million military-product decline primarily from F-16 and a $3.7 million F-16 service decline, with profit impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Program run-off or order delays can reduce normalized anchor OE and make the 0% growth case insufficiently adverse.
audit_findings.evidence: The F-16 program, which consists of multiple production and sustainment contracts, is our largest program and represented 36.7% of our total consolidated net sales in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration is demonstrated, and subsequent filed results show that F-16-related revenue already declined from elevated prior-period levels. The record does not disclose program gross profit or distinguish timing from permanent run-off, so the OE effect remains unresolved. Nevertheless, a program representing more than one-third of FY2025 sales is reasonably capable of materially changing the anchor and valuation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain F-16 product and service gross profit, funded backlog, contract delivery schedules and expected sustainment orders; model temporary timing delays and permanent run-off separately and rerun normalized OE under both cases.
